item.title: Money Managers Say There’s Nowhere to Hide as Super El Niño Forms
item.description: The prospect of the world’s strongest ever El Niño cycle has a growing number of money managers racing to prepare their portfolios for the disruption they say is coming. “There is not a single place in the world that will not feel some kind of a knock-on effect from El Niño.” Strategies to navigate the shocks ahead span bets on interest rates tied to an El Niño-fueled bump in inflation. No corner of global asset markets will be fully shielded from the current El Niño cycle, says Katie Self, a portfolio manager at Pictet Asset Management.

item.title: Tesla Aiming Sell Cybercab Robotaxis by End of Year Despite Federal Probe
item.description: Tesla is aiming to start selling its Cybercab robotaxis to the public by the end of this year, its engineering chief said on Wednesday, even as the US auto safety agency probes the vehicles that come without manual controls which federal regulations typically require. Related: Appeals Court Blocks Class Actions Over Tesla’s Self-Driving Claims “We’re trying to get Cybercabs to customers by the end of this year, 2026,” he said. “As we start small this year, and we learn … about delivery and ownership and fleet management of autonomous vehicles in customer hands, we’ll continue to scale that.” After years of missed promises by Musk, Tesla started offering paid rides on a small fleet of Cybercabs in Austin, Texas, early last month amid a frenzy of fans and social media influencers.

item.title: Critical PHP Flaws Spur Global Patch Effort, Temporary Shutdowns
item.description: Disruption caused by the security issues began Wednesday after researchers disclosed that they had found two critical flaws in PHP that could potentially expose organizations using it in websites and software platforms to cyberattacks. How PHP Flaw Put Millions of Websites, Apps at Risk: Explainer The developers responsible for maintaining PHP released software updates to patch the flaws on Wednesday, urging users to adopt those changes immediately. federal agencies and critical infrastructure firms on the issue.

item.title: Companies, Governments Fight Hacking Attempts in Rush to Patch PHP Flaws
item.description: Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed. As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare. The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand.

item.title: Hawaii Likely Needs $1B in Disaster Recovery, Resilience Funds
item.description: The estimated $686 million in currently identified damage and recovery costs includes: The state has also identified at least $319 million in future resilience and mitigation projects, including: Potential funding sources include federal disaster relief, state insurance, additional appropriations from the Hawaii State Legislature, rainy day funds and revenue from the Green Fee. Current estimates and recovery commitments reported by state agencies total approximately $686 million from the March Kona Low storms, the May 22 magnitude 6.0 Hawaii Island earthquake, Hurricane Lala and Hurricane Lowell, the governor’s statement indicated. The state has also identified at least $319 million in proposed resilience and mitigation projects to strengthen critical infrastructure and prepare Hawaii for future disasters.

item.title: Acquirers Are Snapping Up Boom-Era Startups That Haven’t Raised Funding In Years
item.description: To illustrate the extent to which these aging startups are finding acquirers, we used Crunchbase data to put together a list of 15 deals involving well-funded companies that haven’t raised equity funding for four or more years. As a result, quite a few companies that haven’t raised rounds in years are still chugging along, managing to survive and even grow without more venture funding. This year, a number of larger acquisitions of private companies involved startups that haven’t disclosed a new investment for more than four years.

item.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
item.description: When the NYC pension fund publicly asks you to delay it over AI safety concerns, your chief rival’s CEO calls his own IPO “ill-advised” and postpones it until at least next year, tech stocks are sliding on open-weight model fears, and your own prospectus warns of “existential risks to humanity” from the product you’re selling, that’s not a strategy. Here are the numbers from Anthropic’s leaked prospectus : One more number from the S-1 that the roadshow will bury: A quarter of Anthropic’s 2025 revenue came from two unnamed customers. Last week, the supervisor of New York City’s pension funds — which reportedly hold roughly $7 million in Anthropic exposure today, but could hold dramatically more if Anthropic enters the Russell 3000 post-IPO — sent a letter to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urging the company to pause the IPO entirely.

item.title: Exclusive: Slingshot Raises $27M In Seed Funding To Build An Insurer For Those Small Policies Sold At Checkout
item.description: Slingshot Insurance , an AI-native embedded insurance startup, is emerging from stealth with $27 million in seed funding, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively. Slingshot, which is led by first-time founder and CEO Ethan Genteman , focuses on small insurance policies that consumers can buy as part of another purchase, such as coverage when booking a flight. The startup’s software helps businesses offer those policies by connecting them with insurers that back the coverage.

item.title: Hannover Re raises Acorn Re parametric cat bond target size again, to $450m
item.description: Hannover Re has for a second time increased the target size of what will be the seventh catastrophe bond offering in the annual Acorn Re parametric US earthquake series of deals, now seeking $450 million of limit from the Acorn Re Ltd. Hannover Re returned to market with this new and now seventh Acorn Re parametric catastrophe bond earlier this month , initially seeking $200 million of risk transfer and reinsurance limit for the single named ceding insurer, Oak Tree Assurance Ltd. Now, sources have told us the target size has been further increased, with $450 million of parametric earthquake reinsurance limit now being sought.

item.title: USAA lowers pricing again for still $350m Residential Re 2026-2 cat bond
item.description: US military mutual insurer USAA’s new Residential Reinsurance 2026 Limited (Series 2026-2) catastrophe bond issuance remains at the upsized $350 million target size, but the company seeks to capitalise on investor appetite and has lowered and adjusted the price guidance for the notes on offer again, Artemis has learned. So, the Residential Reinsurance 2026 Limited special purpose vehicle continues to offer three tranches of Series 2026-2 occurrence catastrophe bond notes to investors, with the proceeds set to be used to collateralize underlying reinsurance agreements between the issuing vehicle and sponsor USAA. With USAA once again lowering and adjusting the price of the notes on offer, it clearly shows that the insurer is looking to capitalise on catastrophe bond investor appetite to potentially gain more reinsurance support from the capital markets at more attractive pricing, from its latest cat bond sponsorship.

item.title: Beyond peak risk – The expanding spectrum of diversification in ILS: Artemis London 2026 video
item.description: This third panel session of the day was titled “Beyond peak risk: The expanding spectrum of diversification in ILS.” The discussion was expertly moderated by Harry White , Head of PCS, Verisk Insurance Solutions. This new video features the third panel discussion of the day at our recent Artemis London 2026 catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities conference, a session focused on achieving diversification within the cat bond and ILS asset class and what that actually means for investors. Our Artemis London 2026 conference, the fifth in the series, was held on September 1st and around 220 attendees came through the door on the day to hear a range of insightful discussions from insurance-linked securities and reinsurance market leaders.

item.title: Texas Camp Hit by Floods Must Have New Manager, Judge Says
item.description: Camp Mystic , the Texas girls camp where 28 people were killed in flash floods last summer, must have a new management team to replace the family blamed for the deaths and settle lawsuits filed against the company, a judge ruled. US Bankruptcy Judge Christopher Lopez said that if the family of Richard Eastland, who co-owned and ran the company before he died in the flood, does not agree to give power to settle the lawsuits to an “independent fiduciary” the court will impose a government-approved trustee to run Camp Mystic. Company officials “must now choose whether they will implement independent oversight voluntarily or have the Court appoint a Chapter 11 Trustee.” Lopez rejected two competing proposals for how to manage the conflicts-of-interest involving Eastland family members who manage the camp.

item.title: US Says Screwworm Spreads to Wildlife for First Time
item.description: New World screwworm has been found in an elk in Texas, marking the first confirmed case of the potentially deadly animal parasite in US wildlife. “Hunters and others who spend time outdoors near infested areas are often among the first people to encounter affected wildlife, making their observations especially valuable to surveillance and response efforts,” the USDA said in Wednesday’s statement . Screwworm was first detected in Texas livestock in early June.

item.title: Florida Commissioner Orders Unlicensed Home, Auto Warranty Firms to Cease Ops
item.description: Florida’s insurance commissioner has ordered a home warranty company and an auto warranty firm to cease operations after finding they were not fully licensed in the state. “These suspensions are the result of two market conduct examinations that found iDeal Group, Inc., d/b/a iDeal Auto and First Premier Home Warranty Corp. The home warranty firm had entered into 207 home warranty contracts in Florida in 2023 through 2026, collecting premiums of almost $108,500.

item.title: Brown & Brown introduces COMPASS insurance intelligence platform
item.description: Brown & Brown has introduced COMPASS, an initiative combining its proprietary data, analytics, insurance expertise, and AI capabilities to support risk assessment, insurance purchasing, and portfolio optimisation. The brokerage expects COMPASS-powered knowledge assistants and business intelligence tools to reach thousands of employees by the end of 2026, starting in the US. In another example, the company said COMPASS analytics helped a Fortune 50 customer restructure its insurance program, cutting premium spending by 65% while substantially reducing potential risk volatility.

item.title: Globe Life premiums rise 7% as quarterly profit falls
item.description: Globe Life reported third-quarter net income of $361.1 million, down from $387.8 million a year earlier, while premium revenue rose 7% to $1.31 billion. Health insurance premiums increased 16% to $446.9 million, while life insurance premiums grew 2% to $864.6 million. Globe Life adjusted its full-year 2026 operating earnings guidance to $15.35–$15.65 per share, citing those health insurance issues.

item.title: Introducing Menlo Insurance Services
item.description: Menlo Insurance Services, operated by San Francisco-based Opero Labs, is an independent insurance brokerage offering commercial and personal coverage, with an option to handle insurance quote requests through AI assistants. The brokerage markets coverage including general liability, workers’ compensation, commercial auto, homeowners and specialty insurance for hard-to-place risks. Customers submit their information, and Menlo shops insurers and helps them compare coverage.

item.title: MSI partners with Moved
item.description: MGA MSI announced a new collaboration with Moved, a proptech platform for automating resident moves and ancillary revenue. As part of the partnership, MSI’s renters insurance will be embedded into the Moved platform, and compliance is tracked via the LeaseTrack technology offered through MSI. More than 4,000 properties and over 1 million units nationwide use Moved.

item.title: El Supremo impide que la tasa de incendios municipal opere como una carga propia de las aseguradoras
item.description: La Sala Tercera del Tribunal Supremo ha declarado que los ayuntamientos no pueden exigir a las aseguradoras, por la tasa de prevención y extinción de incendios, una cuota desvinculada de la que corresponde al contribuyente.

item.description: El Instituto Santalucía ha publicado el informe ‘Suecia: el arte de equilibrar pensiones generosas y sostenibles, a través de un sistema multipilar’, elaborado por Fernando Martínez-Cue, socio fundador de Martínez-Cue & Asociados.

item.description: Acrisure España ha incorporado a Grupo X3 Mallorca, compañía balear de servicios de consultoría, formación y prevención de riesgos laborales, en una operación que abre al grupo su entrada en el mercado de las islas.

item.title: GM Targets ‘Eyes-Off’ Autonomous Driving for Pickups, SUVs
item.description: General Motors plans to offer “eyes-off” autonomous driving on its highest-selling, most profitable vehicles — big pickup trucks and SUVs — as it seeks fresh revenue streams from heavy technology investments. Last year, GM said it would offer autonomous highway driving in 2028 on its pricey but light-selling Cadillac Escalade IQ, an electric SUV. Some industry executives have said eyes-off driving that exchanges control back and forth from the car to the driver raises thorny safety and liability questions, and might not interest enough car shoppers.

item.title: Building a Glass Box Not a Black Box at Elara Spatial
item.description: But realizing those gains requires more than adopting new technology, according to Ingrid Flores, CEO of Elara Spatial. For property/casualty insurers seeking to shorten claims cycle times, artificial intelligence offers ample opportunity. Speaking with Carrier Management at the 2026 Insurtech Connect conference in Las Vegas, Flores discussed how her company is approaching property claims automation, why transparency matters, and how she believes insurers could eventually settle catastrophe claims faster with purpose-built AI that meets regulatory requirements.

item.title: Mexico gets its first World Bank Cat DDO, to complement cat bonds and parametric insurance
item.description: The Government of Mexico has received its first World Bank Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO), which will help the country prepare better and respond more quickly to natural disasters, while also complementing both of its IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 and IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) catastrophe bonds and parametric insurance protection. The World Bank Group has approved US $500 million in financing, marking the first time Mexico has accessed a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO). We are proud to support the Government of Mexico in this first Cat DDO,” commented Juan Pablo Uribe, World Bank Director for Mexico, Central America, and the Dominican Republic.

We’ve stayed in touch ever since and I’m really excited that he has agreed to join us to drive our own technology strategy and unlock new opportunities across the delegated authority market.” Basso added, “I’m thrilled to be joining OneAdvent and helping shape its digital future.

item.title: ICEYE to deliver full-lifecycle wildfire intelligence with OroraTech partnership
item.description: ICEYE, a company that operates the world’s largest synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation, has partnered with OroraTech to expand its wildfire intelligence capabilities across the full lifecycle of an event. “Bringing OroraTech’s thermal intelligence together with ICEYE’s SAR capabilities allows us to provide that full-lifecycle view across both the wildland and built environment in one spaceborne solution, giving decision-makers a more complete picture to act on throughout an event.” Dr. The partnership marks a significant expansion of ICEYE’s existing wildfire intelligence offering.

item.title: MSIG UK strengthens executive team with senior underwriting and claims appointments
item.description: Both Harris and Belcourt will take seats on the MSIG UK Executive Committee, bringing their respective underwriting and claims experience to the company’s senior decision-making team. MSIG UK, the UK arm of global insurance group MSIG, has announced two senior appointments as it continues to develop its leadership team and support its long-term business strategy. MSIG UK said her appointment will add further experience to its senior team and support its ongoing focus on claims services for brokers and clients.

item.title: US Urges Fix for Widely Used Software After Critical Alerts
item.description: The US government is working to address and stop any potential cybersecurity issues stemming from flaws in PHP, a widely used open-source software, that may impact federal agencies and American critical infrastructure, according to a White House official. The programming language, called PHP, contains two vulnerabilities which could potentially expose organizations using it in websites and software platforms to cyberattacks. The developers responsible for maintaining PHP said Wednesday they released software updates to patch the vulnerabilities, urging users to adopt those changes immediately.

item.title: The Cost of Losing Your Cool: Tally the Losses of a Supermarket Cyberattack
item.description: Insurance and Financial Implications of France ‘s Supermarket Refrigeration Cyberattack Keeping things cool is generally a good idea in the supermarket business. When a cyberattack reportedly interferes with refrigeration systems, the consequences can extend well beyond a few melted ice creams. The recent incident affecting French supermarkets raises complex questions about insurance coverage and, just as importantly, how to put a price on the resulting financial losses.

item.title: The Latest Launches from Orion180, Arbol, Zywave
item.description: Orion180 Insurance Group Inc., a provider of homeowners and flood insurance, announced the launch of FlexLuxe Homeowners Insurance in certain coastal counties in Florida and throughout Texas. Building on Orion180’s FLEX Home Insurance platform, FlexLuxe offers dwelling coverage of up to $5 million and Total Insured Value of up to $7.5 million. Every policy includes Orion180’s complimentary Automatic Water Turn-Off System, which monitors water flow, pressure and temperature to help reduce the risk of costly water damage.

item.description: (Image source: Roamly website.) Roamly (Austin, Texas) has appointed Christine Franzi Head of Insurance Programs as the company expands insurance offerings for carshare, rideshare, delivery, RV and autonomous fleets across North America and Europe. Christine Franzi, Head of Insurance Programs, Roamly. item.title: Insurity, Coex Partner on Insurance Modernization
item.description: (Image source: Coex website.) Insurity (Hartford, Conn.) has formed a partnership with Coex , a U.K.-based insurance technology consultancy, to support modernization initiatives for insurers, MGAs and InsurTechs across the U.K. The arrangement combines Insurity’s cloud-based insurance software with Coex’s advisory, implementation and change-management capabilities, with an emphasis on reducing execution risk during core-system modernization. “By pairing Insurity’s platform with Coex’s delivery methodology, advisory strength and insurance expertise, we can help organizations move with more clarity, reduce friction during change, and create better outcomes across their operations,” comments Craig Davies, Co-Founder and CEO, Coex.

item.title: Meta to Pay Historic $25 Billion in New Mexico Deception Case
item.description: was ordered to pay a groundbreaking $25 billion civil penalty to the state of New Mexico in a consumer deception case spurred by the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The two-week trial in the First Judicial District Court of New Mexico centered on claims by Attorney General Raúl Torrez (D) that Meta had lied to Facebook users about its privacy policies how it handled their data in the wake of the Cambridge Analytica leak almost a decade ago. But New Mexico has been an especially costly thorn in the side of Meta, opting out of state AG coalitions prosecuting the company and instead going it alone.

item.title: HCI Group expects Isaias losses to impact its reinsurance tower and tokenized securities
item.description: HCI Group, Inc., the insurance holding company, has confirmed that only one of its three reinsurance towers has been impacted after receiving claims from Hurricane Isaias, while the company also expects one of its tokenized reinsurance securities to be affected by losses from the storm too. With respect to the company’s tokenized reinsurance securities, HCI stated that it expects only Token B to be impacted by losses from Hurricane Isaias. HCI said that the impacted reinsurance tower is Reinsurance Tower 3, which covers the northern region of Florida and has a $15 million retention, including participation by the company’s own captive reinsurers.

item.title: Iowa Man Indicted in Ponzi Scheme
item.description: A federal grand jury in Des Moines, Iowa recently returned an indictment charging Willam Bernard Tunink with 10 counts of wire fraud related to a Ponzi scheme involving multiple victims and millions of dollars of loss to the victims. Waterman of the Southern District of Iowa made the announcement. The Iowa Insurance Division’s Fraud Bureau and the Federal Bureau of Investigation are investigating this case.

item.title: Truck Overturns in Kansas City, Spilling Cattle Onto Streets
item.description: Dozens of cattle spilled onto a street in Kansas City, Missouri, when a semitractor-trailer plunged off a highway overpass in the city’s downtown area and onto a car early Sunday, shutting down some roads and setting off a search for the traumatized animals that survived. Some of the cattle had walked several miles before they were captured, said Kansas City Fire Battalion Chief Michael Hopkins. Phil DiMartino said that between 45 and 60 of the 120 to 130 cattle carried by the truck were killed when the tractor trailer overturned and fell from the westbound Interstate 70 curve over southbound I-35.

item.title: Florida AG Says His Office Investigating ‘Anti-Public Adjuster’ Endorsements in Policies
item.description: In the long-simmering clash between property insurers and public adjusters, the adjusters now have Florida’s chief law enforcement officer on their side, after state Attorney General James Uthmeier announced his office will investigate anti-public adjuster endorsements in some Florida insurance policies. Homeowners should be allowed to hire an advocate on their side too.” Uthmeier stated flatly, without attribution: “Homeowners who use a public adjuster can receive up to 30 percent more money on their claims than those who do not.” He may have been referencing a 2010 study from the Florida Office of Program Policy Analysis and Government Accountability, which examined Citizens Property Insurance claims from 2004 and 2005. The report noted that catastrophe claims with public adjuster involvement took four times as long to settle, and that the “typical” PA-involved claim payout was 19% higher in 2004 and 747% higher in 2005.

item.title: The Insurance Alignment Gap: Where Insurer Priorities and Customer Protection Needs Converge…and Diverge
item.description: Based on original research with both insurers and insurance customers, this report examines where priorities align, where they diverge, and how insurers can connect business transformation to customer value. When insurer priorities and customer expectations drift apart, confidence erodes, and so does the opportunity to help customers build financial resilience. Whether you lead strategy, product, distribution, customer experience, or technology, this report offers a research-based view of what customers expect and how your transformation priorities can meet them.

item.title: Government Websites Go Dark As Vulnerabilities in Programming Language Send Shudder Across Internet
item.description: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators scrambling to protect their systems. Developers of the PHP programming language said Tuesday they had identified two critical vulnerabilities and urged users to update their sites as soon as a fix was released. With reports that hackers were already exploiting the flaws to break into websites, government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland were among those that took sites offline as a precaution.

item.title: LA Fire Victims Set to Lose Case Managers Due to Standoff Between California, FEMA
item.description: Now Landau is one of roughly 1,400 households affected by the 2025 Los Angeles fires who are set to lose their disaster case managers by the end of October, as a standoff between California and the Federal Emergency Management Agency over the program’s funding drags on. Case managers simplify a notoriously opaque recovery process Landau kept her insurance policy up to date for the 1938 two-bedroom, one-bathroom ranch home where she raised her three children and tended a wildflower garden. Much of what has sustained her is the encouragement she receives from her disaster case manager.
